title: New USFP Pluggable Optics Form Factor for Higher Speeds from Cisco and NVIDIA
gist: Cisco and NVIDIA are co-developing USFP, a pluggable form factor for 400G-per-lane SerDes enabling 1.6Tbps on four lanes, with an open multi-source spec. Cisco also detailed Silicon One G300/G302/A100L and a SONiC strategy including Live Protect in 2027.

insights.claim: Cisco and NVIDIA are jointly developing USFP, a new ultra-dense small-form-factor pluggable module for 400G SerDes lanes instead of today's common 200G lanes, targeting the 1.6Tbps Ethernet generation.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Next-gen optics form factor is being set by two dominant vendors; optics and module suppliers must align to it.
insights.locator: Cisco and NVIDIA are designing a new pluggable

insights.claim: Moving to 400G lanes allows 1.6Tbps links on four lanes, scaling to 6.4T aggregate across 16 lanes and 12.8T across 32 lanes.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Lane math shows how bandwidth per port scales without proportional port-count growth.

insights.claim: Cisco and NVIDIA are jointly drafting a multi-source specification so other vendors can build USFP modules, and the author expects their backing to make USFP an industry standard.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: A duopoly-backed MSA could shift optics supply chain share and displace QSFP/OSFP roadmaps.
insights.quote: With Cisco and NVIDIA behind USFP, it will become an industry standard.

insights.claim: The author finds it notable that existing QSFP and OSFP form factors were judged insufficient for next-generation speeds, implying a form-factor transition is needed at 400G per lane.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Form-factor resets create openings and risks for incumbent module vendors.
insights.quote: It is interesting that QSFP/ OSFP were not sufficient for the next-gen speeds.
insights.locator: It is interesting that QSFP/ OSFP

insights.claim: Much shipping gear still uses 56G PAM4 and 112G SerDes, so 200G lanes are only 'common' rather than universal and 400G is a long way from volume.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Adoption of 400G lanes is a multi-year transition; near-term revenue stays on older speeds.

themes.theme: Cisco Silicon One switch silicon roadmap

insights.claim: Cisco's Silicon One G300 ships in first Cisco 8000 and N9000 systems at 102.4T capacity across 1.6T ports.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Cisco is competing at the 102.4T tier in AI fabrics against merchant silicon.

insights.claim: Cisco's Silicon One G302 is a 51.2T front-end top-of-rack switch using 200G SerDes, coming in Q4 2026.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Front-end ToR is a volume segment tied to AI cluster build-outs.

themes.theme: Custom silicon in low-end out-of-band switching (A100L)

insights.claim: Cisco's Silicon One A100L applies custom silicon to cost-sensitive 10G/1G out-of-band management switches, whereas custom AI silicon usually appears only in high-performance fabrics where value capture is highest.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Cisco extending custom silicon into low-end switching challenges merchant vendors in a segment viewed as commodity.
insights.quote: A100L sliding into out-of-band management feels almost crazy to me, since the sub-1Tbps switch space was widely assumed to be largely commoditized.

insights.claim: Cisco says A100L proves its architecture scales and that hyperscale customers want to run SONiC on everything, which is its rationale for custom silicon in low-end boxes.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler demand for uniform SONiC stacks may pull vendors into lower-end silicon.

insights.claim: Cisco gave no clear licensing model for A100L (perpetual like C1300 or subscription-like Nexus 9K), and the author argues custom silicon without capturing software revenue versus a merchant part like Marvell Prestera would be a tough road.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Unit economics of A100L hinge on software monetization; watch for licensing disclosure.
insights.quote: if you are doing custom silicon versus like a Marvell Prestera and not capturing software revenue, that feels like a tough road to take.

themes.theme: Cisco SONiC strategy and Live Protect

insights.claim: Cisco's Live Protect for SONiC on Nexus One applies policy to a running N9000 switch for runtime vulnerability shielding before a patch and reboot, with availability slated for Q2 2027 in Cisco-validated SONiC environments.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Reducing patch-window risk is a selling point for enterprise adoption of open-source network OS.

insights.claim: Cisco will offer two SONiC operating models: a community or custom path with full source access, and a turnkey Cisco-validated distribution with a defined upgrade path and professional services.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Validated-distribution services offer Cisco a way to monetize open-source NOS adoption.
insights.locator: An operating-model figure lays out two tracks

insights.claim: Cisco SONiC availability in 2027 is described by the author as a big move for Cisco, and Cisco also continues to support NVIDIA Spectrum-X switching platforms alongside open-source SONiC.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Cisco is hedging across open and NVIDIA ecosystems rather than defending a proprietary stack.
insights.quote: Cisco SONiC is set to be available in 2027, but that feels like a big move for Cisco as well.
